verdict.left_looks: A tall lighthouse-style tower in light grey stone with two bands of red, stepped and slightly leaning, with a dark slate cap and small windows and lantern at the top. At its base is a mossy cobblestone plinth that steps out unevenly. Attached on one side is a low annex with brown timber posts, a salmon-pink plaster wall, a red brick roof and a stone chimney with a torch. The tower has visible stepped and patchy wall sections, and the annex looks cobbled together from mixed materials. Moss and mixed stone read as deliberate weathering.
verdict.right_looks: A tall lighthouse-style tower with clean, straight grey-white walls and two red bands, topped by a dark roof, a glass lantern room and a red cap. It sits on a flat grey stone plinth. A separate timber-framed cottage with a dark brown shingled gable roof, grey plaster walls, dark posts and a stone chimney stands on a grass-and-dirt island edged by water. The layout reads as a coherent lighthouse-and-keeper's-house scene with a clear ground plane.
verdict.why: The right build has cleaner massing, a readable roof and tower silhouette, and a coherent island setting, while the left build's annex and tower base look cobbled together and the stepped walls read as patchy construction rather than character.
